newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Immobilier confirms Cr Foncier role.
newsitem.headline: Cr Immobilier confirms Cr Foncier role.

text.p: France's Credit Immobilier said on Tuesday it had approved plans outlined by the government in July for it to take over the property loans portfolio and some staff of Credit Foncier de France, which is being put in "managed wind-down".

Separately, unions at Credit Foncier said they had drawn up their own plans for the future of the troubled property lender, the second biggest bond issuer in France after the state, and would present them on Wednesday.

Credit Immobilier, a cooperative group dealing mainly in the social housing loans sector, said in a statement it had approved the government proposal and would take over management of a 110 billion franc low-cost PAP loans portfolio as well as taking on 1,500 of some 3,400 Credit Foncier staff.

Under a complicated plan, state bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations is offering 70 francs a share to take over Credit Foncier on the government's behalf, with the cost of a 100 percent buyout put at around 2.5 billion francs.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis has declared Credit Foncier in managed wind-down, with the PAP loans management to be hived off to Credit Immobilier and running of a huge bond issue portfolio to be taken care of by a newly created state holding company.
